result.title: Streaming Tax: Can Streaming VLMs Replace Their Offline Parents?
result.summary: Most vision-language models (VLMs) specialize in offline video understanding; in contrast, their post-trained versions, streaming VLMs, can perform live interactions. We investigate whether streaming VLMs can replace their offline parent models on offline tasks. Such replacement could reduce deployment costs and improve efficiency. We propose Streaming Tax to systematically evaluate streaming VLMs on offline tasks. Our exploration spans three core dimensions: understanding, trustworthiness, and generalization across 15 benchmarks. Our findings reveal a critical gap between offline capability preservation and practical replaceability. This gap emerges at two stages: streaming adaptation can alter trustworthy behavior even when offline understanding is largely preserved, while the native streaming protocol can introduce further performance losses. Our analyses show that some of these losses arise from restricted access to historical visual evidence and failures to deliver usable responses. Importantly, regarding safety, streaming models often leave both harmful and legitimate requests unanswered rather than genuinely refusing unsafe ones. We then propose Stream++, a training-free plugin to improve streaming VLMs on offline tasks.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 Streaming Tax，在 15 个基准上从理解、可信度与泛化三个维度，系统检验 streaming VLM 能否在离线任务上替代其 offline 父模型，并分析性能损失来源，最后给出免训练插件 Stream++。
AI.relevance_reason: 其对「历史视觉证据访问受限」与安全请求未被真正拒绝的失败分析，可供核查 LVR 中视觉细节能否保留在内部状态、证据获取成本与停止决策等问题；但未涉及 latent 推理状态的生成，联系偏诊断层面。
